newsitem.title: EGYPT: Mutual funds prop up Egypt share prices.
newsitem.headline: Mutual funds prop up Egypt share prices.

text.p: Egyptian share prices edged higher on Wednesday as local and international mutual funds swooped down on the market, pumping turnover to a two-week high.
The Capital Market Authority (CMA) said its all-share index inched 0.9 percent to 382.36 points in heavy turnover worth 117.33 million pounds ($34.56 million), its highest level since March 24.

"The funds are the most active traders on the market and we're seeing more volume now. They see the market as attractive and they're no longer net buyers or net sellers. It's very healthy," said broker Sherif Cararah of EFG/Hermes.
Smaller investors, he said, were still sidelined and were waiting for prices to pick up a little more after the recent correction.

Cararah said that the funds were behind three-quarters of the share blocks that made up Wednesday's trading and broker Khaled Adly of El Rashad Securities Brokerage said American Express Bank's newly-established 300 million pound fund was the main player.
"Amex are building their portfolio and buying into everything, cements and mills in particular. They are also responsible for the movement in the government bonds," he said.
The normally static housing bonds made up about 28,935 pounds of turnover and ended mixed.

The day's most active share was Helwan Portland Cement, which also topped Tuesday's trading. The share ended unchanged at 79 pounds after trading worth 14.24 million pounds. Amriyah Cement was busy too, with shares worth 4.5 million trading and the stock also ended unchanged at 86 pounds.

Partly private Alexandria Commercial and Maritime Bank had the second heaviest turnover at 13.5 million pounds and brokers said it was made up by the bank's goverment shareholders selling chunks to each other.
The state last week offered private investors an initial 20,400 share tranche of its stake in the joint venture bank on Monday and Tuesday. Brokers said the agents were still gathering buying orders.
The shares represents 1.8 percent of Alexandria Commercial and Maritime's total 1.125 million shares and the stock ended 7.18 pounds higher at 150.81.

Other "collectables" were mainly in the milling sector. North Cairo Flour Mills came up top with 2.7 million shares worth of trade but ended one pound higher at 191. Upper Egypt Flour Mills rose 0.1 to 89.1.

Brokers said the funds were also targetting fertiliser firms like Egyptian Financial and Industrial and Abu Qir Fertiliser and Chemicals. Other popular stocks included Eipico/Egyptian International Pharmaceutical Industries and other drugs companies, although the state has said it would not give up control of the firms because of their "strategic" nature.
The index for openly traded firms rose to 585.54 points from 573.5 points on Tuesday and the index for rarely traded "closed" firms also rose to 266.08 from 265.6 points.
Out of the 84 shares traded, 37 gained, 19 lost and 28 ended unchanged.
